cards.headline: PWD Floats Tenders for Nine New Bridges Across Udupi District
cards.body: The Public Works Department (PWD) has officially floated tenders for the construction and reconstruction of nine bridges across Udupi district. These bridge projects aim to improve rural and semi-urban connectivity, replace deteriorating structures, and withstand heavy monsoon flows along coastal river stretches. The tender process sets the stage for civil engineering works, demanding substantial quantities of structural steel, ready-mix concrete, stone aggregate, and specialized civil construction materials.
cards.impact_text: Local contractors and building material suppliers can prepare bids and credit lines to supply TMT rebar, cement, and aggregates for these upcoming civic works.

cards.headline: NTT DATA Plans Major Tech Expansion in Mangaluru and Udupi
cards.body: Global IT services provider NTT DATA is exploring significant operations expansion across coastal Karnataka, targeting Mangaluru and Udupi as secondary technology hubs. Company leadership met with Karnataka IT-BT Minister Priyank Kharge to discuss infrastructure requirements, talent availability, and government support. The expansion aims to decongest Bengaluru by establishing regional digital campuses, which is expected to boost commercial real estate, office space leasing, and high-quality commercial interior fit-outs in the coastal belt.
cards.impact_text: Growth in regional corporate offices drives medium-term demand for commercial building hardware, electricals, architectural fittings, and residential housing in Udupi district.

cards.headline: Karnataka Government Unveils Rs 16,000 Crore Infrastructure Package for Coastal Districts
cards.body: The Karnataka Cabinet held discussions to prioritize coastal infrastructure, announcing development projects worth Rs 16,000 crore for Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts. The major package focuses on upgrading state highways, drainage networks, coastal sea-wall protection, port connectivity, and urban civic amenities. State ministers emphasized fast-tracking local infrastructure works to stimulate economic activity, improve regional freight logistics, and support climate-resilient civil construction across the sensitive coastal belt.
cards.impact_text: Massive state funding into coastal civil works guarantees steady institutional demand for cement, structural steel, and drainage pipes across regional supply chains.

cards.headline: Prime Minister Inaugurates India's Largest Underground LPG Storage Cavern in Mangaluru
cards.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has inaugurated India's largest underground LPG storage cavern facility in Mangaluru. Built at significant capital expenditure, this mega underground facility provides strategic energy reserves, bolstering LPG supply security across southern India and regional industrial zones. The massive cavern project enhances Mangaluru's standing as a pivotal coastal energy and industrial corridor, expanding regional heavy logistics networks and industrial ancillary operations along the Karnataka coast.
cards.impact_text: Strengthens coastal Karnataka's industrial infrastructure profile, driving sustained logistics activity and long-term industrial construction in the Mangaluru-Udupi corridor.

cards.headline: South Western Railway Fast-Tracks Coastal Rail Infrastructure and Mangaluru Facility Upgrades
cards.body: South Western Railway (SWR) authorities conducted high-level inspections across Mangaluru rail facilities following the Centre's reaffirmation to strengthen coastal railway networks. With the launch of the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express and ongoing integration demands, commercial passenger and freight infrastructure is set for modern upgrades. Railway development forums noted that consolidating coastal rail under unified management will eliminate decades of logistical bottlenecks, improving cargo movement and passenger connectivity between coastal Karnataka and the hinterland.
cards.impact_text: Upgraded rail freight terminals and faster connections to Bengaluru reduce logistics turnaround times for bulk materials like cement, tiles, and steel entering coastal Karnataka.

cards.headline: Indian Steel Mills Face Margin Squeeze as Coking Coal Costs Spike
cards.body: Primary domestic steelmakers including JSW Steel are warning of squeezed operating margins due to a sudden surge in imported coking coal prices. While sluggish domestic festive demand caused localized softening in spot prices for coated and billet steel, industry analysts project primary mills may soon push price hikes of up to Rs 2,000 per tonne to offset raw material inflation. The cost pressures create immediate divergence between weak spot demand and rising factory-gate production costs.
cards.impact_text: Anticipate a possible Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,000 per tonne hike in primary TMT rebar and coil prices; balance retail inventory without over-committing to high-cost stock.

cards.headline: Centre to Examine Non-GST Levies on Steel to Improve Market Competitiveness
cards.body: The central government has agreed to examine various non-GST levies, cesses, and royalty burdens imposed on the domestic steel industry. Domestic steelmakers have urged the Ministry of Steel to rationalize local resource taxation, mining charges, and logistics surcharges that sit outside the GST credit mechanism. Lowering these embedded levies aims to curb domestic production expenses, make domestic steel competitive against cheap foreign imports, and stabilize retail prices across construction supply chains.
cards.impact_text: Rationalization of outside-GST mining and transport levies could curb input costs for steel producers, helping stabilize long-term distributor billing prices.

cards.headline: Domestic Steel Consumption Expands 7.5% to 99.4 MT as Imports Surge Nearly 29%
cards.body: India’s finished steel consumption expanded 7.5% year-on-year to reach 99.4 million tonnes during the April–October period, driven by ongoing infrastructure projects and building activity. However, steel imports surged 28.9% over the same timeframe, as cheaper overseas supplies from China and other Asian producers entered the domestic market. The strong influx of imported steel continues to suppress domestic manufacturer pricing power despite healthy construction sector consumption.
cards.impact_text: Robust domestic demand keeps project construction moving, but higher import volumes are preventing sudden price spikes, keeping inventory acquisition costs stable.

cards.headline: US Proposes 25% Tariffs on Indian Exports Citing Manufacturing Overcapacity
cards.body: The United States Trade Representative has proposed new tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, alleging that subsidies under 'Make in India' and Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes create artificial manufacturing overcapacity. Indian trade bodies and export federations warned that duties could threaten $48 billion in exports, though negotiated concessions could lower rates to 17%. The Union Commerce Ministry is reviewing the allegations, maintaining that domestic incentives comply with international trade rules.
cards.impact_text: If export tariffs hurt Indian heavy manufacturing, producers may divert more factory output into the domestic market, altering domestic pricing dynamics.
